resources.fullDescription: Our EATS Program takes place Monday through Friday from 11:00 AM'12:00 PM. During this time, we serve meals to all neighbors who walk through our doors in an effort to help reduce food insecurity within our community. Every Friday before closing, we also stock our Blessing Box with nonperishable food items to assist neighbors throughout the weekend when lunch services are unavailable. Our LIVES Program focuses on providing essential support services and resources to individuals and families in need. On the first Monday of every month, we distribute hygiene bags for men and women. We also assist with housing resources, healthcare resources, SNAP benefits paperwork, job resources, and referrals for financial assistance through our community partners. Our PRAYS Program is centered around providing spiritual support and encouragement to our neighbors. We have partnered with several local churches whose members visit during our EATS Program to socialize with neighbors and offer prayer and encouragement to those who wish to participate. LEARNS Program is designed for teens and grade school students. On Wednesdays, we host our Teen Sessions where we discuss important life skills such as career planning, car ownership, academic success, and other topics that prepare youth for the future. Each teen also receives a meal to take home for themselves and their family. On Thursdays, we host our LEARNS Scholar Sessions. We begin with Bible study and outdoor activities before transitioning into our afterschool literacy tutoring program. Volunteers read with the scholars, and students then create and present speeches in front of tutors and peers to help improve literacy skills, confidence, and public speaking abilities. Each scholar also receives a large meal to take home for themselves and their family.

resources.address: 3319 Old Pond Road, Johns Island, SC 29455
resources.shortDescription: This six-week training course offers a practical, hands-on pathway to stable employment and recovery by teaching carpentry and basic…
resources.fullDescription: This six-week training course offers a practical, hands-on pathway to stable employment and recovery by teaching carpentry and basic construction skills through the design and building of tiny homes. It is designed specifically for people reentering the community after incarceration and for those working to overcome substance use challenges. The program combines vocational training, life skills, and supportive services to promote long-term success. $200/week, job placement after the program, some sort of ID required for intake, they will help with other forms (prison ID works) What you’ll learn Core carpentry skills: measuring, cutting, framing, sheathing, roofing, siding, and basic finish work. Construction basics: tool safety and maintenance, reading simple plans, material selection, and jobsite workflows. Tiny home-specific techniques: space-saving design, modular construction, insulating small structures, and basic utility integration (plumbing and electrical overview for safe coordination with licensed trades). Soft skills and workplace readiness: punctuality, teamwork, communication, resume writing, job search strategies, and interview practice. Recovery and reentry supports: relapse prevention strategies, peer support, accessing treatment and community resources, and legal/records navigation.
